fix: timezone plugin: .tz() reuses one cached Intl.DateTimeFormat per zone instead of calling Date#toLocaleString (which builds a new formatter every call). About 5-6x faster per .tz() call with identical results.
credit: @logeyG (PR #2019 author; Co-authored-by in the fork commit)
changes: src/plugin/timezone/index.js -> plugin/timezone.js and esm/plugin/timezone/index.js: cached formatter (getLocaleStringifier from PR #2019) with exactly toLocaleString()'s default options, so the formatted string is identical. The PR's unrelated options refactor was not applied (it no longer applied cleanly).
Every other built file is byte-identical to the published dayjs@1.11.23 tarball (locale.json differs only in entry order).
verification: Formatter output equals Date#toLocaleString for 37,200 timestamps x 8 zones.
Benchmark: 20,000 x dayjs(t).tz(zone): about 300 ms vs about 1,700 ms for upstream 1.11.23 (x5.8), identical formatted results.

Upstream timezone tests pass in 4 TZs (54/54 each); full jest suite 792/794 with the 2 failures (localizedFormat, dayOfYear) identical on unmodified 1.11.23 when TZ=America/New_York and passing with TZ=UTC.
